1.why: B is the 'X, not Y' corrective reframe; D is an absolute ('Nothing ... was worth keeping') and A is its unqualified mirror.

2.why: Among three listener-results D is the only asymmetric directional finding; A is the null, B is off-axis, C swaps the actor to speakers.

3.why: C is the hedged qualifier ('may fail ... when underlying conditions are unaddressed'); D is the absolute 'no relationship at all' and B the reversed-cause bait.

4.why: Betting the undramatic gradual-decline option against two catastrophe options (attack, population crash); no prose tell, prior only.

5.why: D is the only option stating a specific result plus the inference it licenses ('implying ...'); A and B are generic hedges about drugs in general.

6.why: C is the only option carrying a matched control comparison (risky vs comparably reachable safe sites), the shape a command-of-evidence key takes.

7.why: D is the 'rather than' reframe; A is an absolute ('cannot'), B a flat endorsement, C a generic value judgement.

8.why: B is the counterexample to the origin-predicts-harm claim that item 13's key also attacks; C and D are the survey-generalization cast.

9.why: A is the only option that removes the body-size confound rather than restating it; B and C both merely describe the largest species.

10.why: B is the hedged 'cannot by itself settle' qualifier against 'proves' (A) and 'definitively traced' (D).

11.why: A is the plain benefit explanation; C is an absolute ('of any use'), D attributes the behavior to ignorance, B inverts the causal direction.

12.why: A is the general evolutionary principle; B is Lamarckian, C a reversed cost claim, D an absolute ('every environment ... included').

13.why: C is the corrective/misdirection reframe ('origin, rather than actual effect'); D is a flat rejection and B an overreaching 'usually enrich'.

14.why: A is the scoped partial concession ('rotation curves alone do not compel'); B accepts fully, C and D are 'at every scale'/'at any scale' absolutes.

15.why: B is the exception-to-a-general-rule purpose; A is the unqualified 'reliably narrows', C an absolute 'no effect ... any risk', D a too-narrow topic.

16.why: D is the positive order-preserving finding; A, B and C are its three systematic negations (wrong order, silence, no-learning control).

17.why: C is the 'reflects X rather than Y' reframe of what the record measures; D is the absolute 'insignificant' and B a motive-attribution.

18.why: B and C are a near-duplicate pair differing on one fact; betting the internally consistent correlational reading over the 'yet' contrast.

19.why: C is the strong-version-replaced-by-weaker structure (concede then qualify); D ends in 'refutes it entirely' and B in endorsing neither.

20.why: D is the only option with an experimental contrast against an untouched control condition; A, B, C are single-factor generalities.

21.why: A is the 'deliberate rather than incidental' reframe; B and D both hang on 'inevitably', C asserts a flat incapacity.

22.why: B is the hedged counterintuitive claim ('may diverge more'); D is the absolute 'always inaccurate' and A/C the storage-model opposites.

23.why: Coin flip between A's full causal chain and D's 'even as' regional contrast; betting the mechanism-stating option, no prose tell separates them.

24.why: A is the hedged 'can reinforce rather than revise'; D is the absolute 'no power to change anyone's mind' and B the deficit-model opposite.
